meta.name: Raking Light
meta.notes: Porcelain-white relief owns the mood; --c-primary appears only on prices (mixed toward ink for contrast), the cart count, primary buttons and pressed/active states.

issues: Creativity 7: the raking-light relief model is fully implemented and gives a real tactile identity, but the static shots read as tasteful neumorphism.
Typography 7: thin Piazzolla display is elegant. The hero lede and USP copy are tiny, low-contrast muted grey and almost disappear.
Layout 7: calm 3-column tile grid. Without prices every tile's buy row is an empty left side with a lonely 42px '+' circle, so the bottom third of each tile looks unfinished.
Polish 6: the 'Added to your cart' toast with an empty name shows up permanently in the full-page shots (hidden only by translateY, which fails when the viewport is tall).
Brand robustness 8: TeleQare's purple and Nacra's orange both sit well because colour is limited to the CTA, cart and eyebrow dot.
Mobile 7: the nav row is clipped mid-word ('CO') with no hint that it scrolls, and the price-less tiles have the same empty buy row.
Generic-ness: moderate. The relief light keeps it from being a stock template, but the empty tile footers make it look like a placeholder grid.
fixed: Tile add-to-cart is now a raised, labelled pill ('In winkelwagen', localized). With a price it sits right of the price. Without one, the empty price is collapsed and the pill anchors the row. On mobile it becomes a full-width pressed-in-on-click pill when there is no price, or stays an icon next to the price. Same on home and catalog.
Toast is also hidden with opacity/visibility, so it never leaks into the page or into screenshots when idle. The slide-in is kept.
Mobile nav gets a soft right-edge fade mask so the horizontal scroll reads as intentional instead of clipped text.
Hero lede is larger (15–17px), with tighter measure and much higher contrast. USP body copy also gets more contrast, so the quiet palette stays readable.
Added state on the pill tints the check in --c-primary and hover tints the label, keeping colour limited to active states as the brief asks.
